question: Why should a performance review session be a two-way conversation?

options.C: It ensures the manager does not have to prepare any written notes

question: What is an immunization defaulter?

options.B: A parent who refuses all medical treatments
options.C: A health worker who forgets to order vaccines
options.D: An infant who experiences a mild vaccine reaction

explanation: A defaulter simply refers to a child who fails to show up for a scheduled vaccine or misses a dose needed to complete their immunization schedule. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h1)

question: About how many centimeters is the diaphragm pushed upward during pregnancy?

options.A: Twelve centimeters
options.B: One centimeter
options.C: Four centimeters
options.D: Ten centimeters

question: What is the main goal of birth preparedness and complication readiness in pregnancy?

options.A: To eliminate the need for routine antenatal visits
options.B: To choose the exact time and date of labor
options.C: To remove delays in accessing emergency obstetric care
options.D: To guarantee a home delivery without any skilled staff

question: Which of these is NOT a mechanical complication caused by high pressure settings on a ventilator?

options.A: Subcutaneous emphysema in the neck

options.C: Pneumothorax from alveolar rupture
options.D: Tension pneumothorax development

explanation: Spot on! Pneumonia is an infection caused by germs, whereas things like a collapsed lung (pneumothorax) happen from high pressure popping the delicate air sacs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T18#GNS213_U2_T18_h6)

question: What is a core feature of critical thinking in nursing?

options.A: Questioning assumptions and weighing clinical evidence
options.B: Relying solely on what was memorized in school
options.C: Avoiding complex patient care assignments
options.D: Accepting every doctor's order without question

explanation: Critical thinking requires looking deeper into a situation rather than just accepting surface-level appearances. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why do we often use a mix of different therapies to manage chronic pain in patients with physical disabilities?

options.A: Single medications are completely ineffective for all types of nerve pain
options.B: Non-pharmacological methods remove the need for any clinical supervision
options.C: Combining different therapies addresses multiple underlying causes of pain safely
options.D: Pain associated with physical disabilities always resolves spontaneously

explanation: Chronic pain has many layers, so combining meds and physical therapy gives better relief without needing dangerously high drug doses. Smart approach! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T15#GNS225_U5_T15_h6)

question: Why is a quiet, private environment essential when a nurse conducts a telehealth video call?

options.A: To make the nurse's computer battery last much longer during the shift
options.B: To stop other staff members from asking questions about their work
options.C: To ensure compliance with patient privacy and confidentiality laws
options.D: To prevent background noise from interrupting the internet signal

explanation: Conducting calls in private spaces stops unauthorized people from overhearing sensitive health discussions, protecting patient confidentiality. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why do we use the nursing diagnosis 'Fatigue' for someone with anemia?

options.A: To ensure the patient stays on strict bed rest all day
options.B: To prove the patient is not sleeping well at night
options.C: To address reduced oxygen-carrying capacity in the blood
options.D: To document that the patient is refusing hospital food

explanation: Anemia means fewer red blood cells to ferry oxygen around. Less oxygen means less energy for the body—hence, deep fatigue! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h3)

question: How do conference presentations differ from traditional journal articles?

options.A: They allow researchers to share findings much faster than waiting for print
options.B: They require strict peer review by government panels before submission
options.C: They focus exclusively on financial accounting instead of patient outcomes
options.D: They prevent the audience from asking questions about the study

explanation: Because journal publication takes many months, conferences provide a much quicker route to air new data. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is considered the most powerful tool for breaking down mental health stigma in communities?

options.A: Strict laws that fine people for speaking about mental illness
options.B: Personal contact and storytelling from people with lived experience
options.C: Locking away individuals who show signs of mental distress
options.D: Hiding psychiatric clinics behind high, secret walls

explanation: Hearing real recovery stories humanizes mental illness and shatters the false stereotypes that fuel community stigma. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h6)

question: How do you handle the assessment phase during a tele-nursing consultation?

options.A: By relying heavily on verbal descriptions, patient self-reports, and transmitted media
options.B: By reviewing only the physician's past medical history notes
options.C: By skipping physical checks entirely and guessing the diagnosis
options.D: By forcing every patient to travel to the central lab immediately

explanation: Good thinking! Since you can't touch the patient physically, you rely on smart questioning, listening closely, and checking photos or videos they send you. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h4)

question: How does individualizing a medication schedule help a patient?

options.A: It allows the nurse to finish the shift much earlier
options.B: It lowers the financial cost of buying the medications from the pharmacy
options.C: It fits the drug timing into their normal daily routine to prevent missed doses
options.D: It stops the drug from causing any side effects in the body

explanation: When drugs match a person's daily habits, they are much easier to remember and take consistently. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why are normal losses from breathing and light sweating called insensible fluid losses?

options.A: They only happen when the patient is unconscious
options.B: They do not affect the body's overall fluid balance
options.C: They cannot be measured directly with standard equipment
options.D: They are completely harmless to the human body

explanation: Insensible losses evaporate continuously into the air and through the skin without leaving a pool of liquid to measure. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h4)

question: How does the body react when you consistently take in fewer calories than it burns?

options.A: It immediately stops producing insulin
options.B: It taps into stored energy reserves
options.C: It increases daily resting bone density
options.D: It permanently shuts down digestion

explanation: You've got it! When energy intake drops, the body naturally looks at its stored fat and glycogen to keep running smoothly. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T010#GNS227_U6_T010_h1)

question: What is the primary name of the smooth muscle that forms the wall of the urinary bladder?

options.A: Detrusor muscle
options.B: Sphincter muscle
options.C: Urethral muscle
options.D: Pelvic floor muscle

explanation: The detrusor muscle makes up the main muscular wall of the bladder and contracts to push urine out during urination. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h2)

question: Why is communication considered a vital part of the IEC approach rather than just giving information?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will take their prescribed medications on time.
options.B: It establishes a two-way dialogue to build trust and address community concerns.
options.C: It allows the nurse to avoid writing formal health reports.
options.D: It eliminates the need for any formal health education classes.

explanation: Communication is a two-way process that fosters trust and helps health workers understand local beliefs and fears. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h1)

question: What do we call the action where food is pushed back inside the stomach to get mashed up even more?

options.A: Peristalsis
options.B: Retropulsion
options.C: Regurgitation
options.D: Segmentation

explanation: Think of retropulsion as the stomach's bounce-back action. Food gets pushed toward the closed exit valve and bounces back for another round of mixing! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T3#GNS121_U1_T3_h4)

question: What factor most determines what kind of birth defect a teratogen will cause?

options.A: Whether the placenta is anterior or posterior
options.B: Total volume of amniotic fluid present
options.C: Gestational age at the time of exposure
options.D: The mother's blood type and Rhesus factor

explanation: Brilliant! Timing is everything because different organs develop at different weeks; exposure during organogenesis causes structural issues, while later exposure affects growth. You nailed it! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T005#GNS226_U2_T005_h7)

question: Which of these is an example of a physical 'forcing function' that protects patient safety?

options.A: Designing feeding tubes that cannot physically plug into intravenous IV lines
options.B: Writing a strict policy warning staff about the dangers of drug errors
options.C: Requiring nurses to double-check every single medication calculation verbally
options.D: Punishing any nurse who fails to report a near-miss incident on the ward

explanation: A forcing function makes it physically impossible to do the wrong thing—like making connectors that only fit the correct equipment! [learn more](GST319_U2_T2#GST319_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why do many families in Nigeria often turn to traditional care first when a loved one shows signs of mental illness?

options.A: Deep-rooted cultural philosophies and beliefs
options.B: Mandatory government healthcare policies
options.C: Strict orders from orthodox medical doctors
options.D: A complete absence of spiritual practices

explanation: You've got this! Cultural views deeply shape how communities understand illness, making traditional care a familiar and trusted first step for many families. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T2#GNS314_U4_T2_h1)

question: A patient admitted for severe hyperemesis is about to receive IV glucose fluids. Why must she receive thiamine (Vitamin B1) first?

options.A: To help the liver process the incoming sugar more quickly
options.B: To prevent Wernicke's encephalopathy from vitamin deficiency
options.C: To prevent allergic reactions to the plastic IV tubing
options.D: To stop the patient from feeling sleepy during the infusion

explanation: Great catch! Giving sugar to a malnourished patient without thiamine can trigger a serious brain complication called Wernicke's encephalopathy. Always protect the brain first! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h5)

question: What is the name of the dilated pouch just beneath the nipple where milk pools?

options.A: Lactiferous sinus
options.B: Alveolar duct
options.C: Lymphatic vessel
options.D: Sebaceous pouch

explanation: The lactiferous sinus acts as a temporary reservoir for milk right before it reaches the nipple pores during feeding. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h4)

question: What is a major structural difference between sympathetic and parasympathetic pathways?

options.A: Sympathetic fibers never use ganglia to pass signals along.
options.B: Sympathetic preganglionic fibers are always much longer than postganglionic fibers.
options.C: Parasympathetic nerves only exit through the lumbar spinal cord.
options.D: Parasympathetic ganglia are usually located close to or inside the target organs.

explanation: Because parasympathetic fibers travel a long way from the brain or lower spine before reaching their destination, their relay stations (ganglia) sit right near or inside the target organ walls. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h2)

question: In midwifery, what is the medical term for a normal, uncomplicated vaginal delivery?

options.A: Dystocia
options.B: Cephalopelvic disproportion
options.C: Placenta praevia
options.D: Eutocia

question: Why aren't standard antibody blood tests ideal for diagnosing an active case of onchocerciasis?

options.B: They require frozen tissue samples to function
options.C: They show past exposure rather than current infection
options.D: They cannot detect any immune response in humans

explanation: Antibodies stick around in the blood long after the body has dealt with the parasite. A positive blood test just means past exposure, not necessarily an active worm load right now. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T7#GNS214_U1_T7_h4)

question: What should you do as a nurse if your home care plan isn't giving the results you hoped for?

options.A: Continue the exact same steps without making changes
options.B: Discharge the client from home care immediately
options.C: Wait until the client is admitted to the hospital
options.D: Revise the care plan with the interdisciplinary team

explanation: Brilliant! Nursing care is dynamic. If something isn't working, we team up and adjust the plan to better help our client. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T3#GNS324_U1_T3_h7)

question: How many unique identifiers must you use to make sure you have the right patient?

options.A: Three completely different family members
options.B: Only one verbal confirmation
options.C: At least two unique identifiers
options.D: No identifiers if you already know them

explanation: Always check at least two things—like their name and hospital ID band—even if you know their face well. It's a quick habit that prevents big mix-ups! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T1#GNS125_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why do nurses use slide sheets when moving a patient from a bed to a stretcher?

options.A: They replace the need for any nurses to assist
options.B: They act as a heating pad to warm up the patient
options.C: They automatically record the patient's weight
options.D: They reduce friction and shearing forces on the patient's skin

explanation: Slide sheets are a nurse's best friend! They make patients glide smoothly, protecting fragile skin from friction and saving your back from strain. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h8)

question: Which of these nursing actions is a classic example of primary prevention?

options.A: Managing blood pressure medications for hypertension
options.B: Screening adult patients for elevated blood glucose
options.C: Providing physical therapy after a stroke occurs
options.D: Administering the measles vaccine to school children

question: What defense mechanism is happening when someone takes their frustration out on a safer, less threatening target?

options.A: Rationalization
options.B: Denial
options.C: Displacement
options.D: Projection

question: What is a common potential complication following rectovaginal fistula repair?

question: What is the primary purpose of secondary neurological prevention?

options.B: Performing major neurosurgery in emergency rooms
options.C: Preventing people from ever starting to smoke
options.D: Teaching chronic patients how to use a wheelchair

explanation: Secondary prevention is all about early catch-up. Through quick screenings and fast intervention, we catch health issues early to limit lasting damage. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T24#GNS222_U3_T24_h3)

question: Why is it important to involve men and boys in community GBV prevention programs?

question: A patient is given timolol eye drops for glaucoma. How do these drops actually lower eye pressure?

options.B: By widening the tear drainage system
options.C: By completely relaxing the outer eye muscles
options.D: By decreasing the production of fluid (aqueous humor)

question: How did the role of the nurse change with the introduction of coronary care units?

options.A: Nurses were trained to independently spot dangerous rhythms and start emergency defibrillation

options.C: Nurses focused solely on administering oral medications prescribed at shift change
options.D: Nurses were restricted from touching cardiac monitors without direct written doctor orders

question: How did the introduction of psychotropic medications change inpatient psychiatric units?

options.C: It caused patients to lose all of their memories permanently
options.D: It completely eliminated the need for psychiatric nurses

question: What is another name for the sympathetic division based on where its nerves leave the spinal cord?

question: What is the main goal of preventive reproductive health services?

options.D: To manage high-risk surgical emergencies in labor wards

question: Which laboratory test results should a nurse check first to see how well a patient's kidneys are clearing drugs?

question: What is a major drawback of relying too much on private healthcare in developing economies?

question: What do home ovulation predictor kits mainly test for in urine?

question: When is total parenteral nutrition (feeding directly into the veins) specifically needed?

question: Which gland pumps adrenaline (epinephrine) straight into the blood during a scare?

question: A patient with severe kidney failure is prescribed a magnesium-based laxative. What is the best nursing action?

question: A nurse reads a study and wonders if the results can safely apply to patients in her own local hospital. Which concept is she checking?

question: How does psychoeducation benefit families of clients with mental health conditions?

options.B: It empowers them with knowledge about the illness and how to handle crises effectively
options.C: It completely eliminates all stressful events from their household

question: To be most effective after an unprotected sexual assault, within how many hours should emergency contraception be given?

question: What is a long-term health benefit for a woman who practices exclusive breastfeeding?

question: Why must you always have a transport plan in place before attending a home birth?

question: What is the biggest reason why survivors of violence often find it hard to speak up right away?

options.A: Forgetfulness
options.B: Strict hospital policies
options.C: Lack of symptoms

question: What is a major spatial or geographical challenge for patients living in remote rural areas?

question: How often should a bedridden stroke patient be repositioned to prevent pressure ulcers?

question: What is the main focus of a maternity home in the community?

options.A: Managing low-risk pregnancies and normal deliveries
options.B: Treating chronic illnesses in elderly patients
options.C: Performing major complex obstetric surgeries
options.D: Providing long-term pediatric intensive care

question: What actually happens during a drug interaction?

question: What do the letters PDSA stand for in quality improvement?

options.D: Practice, Document, Share, Apply

question: A patient reports waking up three times every night to pass urine. What term should the nurse document?

question: Why should hospital waste bags be tied up when they are only three-quarters full?

question: What is the main danger when food or liquid silently slips into a patient's lungs without them even coughing?

question: What is the main job of micronutrients in the human body?

options.C: Storing excess body fat for warmth
options.D: Regulating chemical reactions and body processes

question: What is the first phase of the nursing process?

question: What is a common, dangerous mistake when handing out crutches or walking sticks to injured people in a disaster?

question: In nutritional psychiatry, what does the 'gut-brain axis' mean?

question: Why is the research-practice gap a serious concern in nursing?

question: Which health areas are most commonly supported by international donors and NGOs in Nigeria?

question: When are most anthelminthic drugs strictly avoided due to risks to the baby?

question: A clinic is near a busy highway and a river that floods easily. Who should nurses prioritize first when planning an evacuation?

question: Why does a full bladder often make postpartum bleeding worse?

question: What exactly is a 'maternal near miss'?

question: In newly arrived displaced populations, which health issues are most commonly reported?

question: How does school-based health education impact the wider community?

question: What is the primary focus of medical services for special children?

question: Which organ is primarily responsible for filtering waste products from the blood to produce urine?

question: A nurse designs a questionnaire for depression, but the questions only ask about lack of sleep. What is the main problem here?

question: What is the main goal of doing a root cause analysis after an incident like a patient fall?

question: What is the absolute first thing you must do when an adverse event happens?

question: Which type of healthcare standard looks closely at a hospital's physical environment and tools?

question: What is considered an immunization error-related adverse event?

question: When you swallow a pill, where does it start undergoing metabolism before it even reaches the rest of the body?

question: Which embryonic germ layer develops into the nervous system and the outer skin?

question: What happens if a bar chart's vertical scale doesn't start at zero?

question: Which of these is a major cause of population displacement in northeast Nigeria?

question: When a patient needs both a bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid, why should the bronchodilator be used first?

question: What is the primary function of lysozyme found in tears?

question: Which infection is commonly spread through sharing unsterilized needles for drug injection?

question: A patient calls the clinic panicking because their stool turned dark green after starting iron pills. What should you tell them?

question: How do membrane filters clean liquid solutions of microorganisms?

question: Why does sudden, heavy bleeding (acute blood loss) often cause tachycardia?

question: A nurse uses a bedside scanner to check a patient's wristband and a medication package before giving a pill. What safety feature is being used?

question: A nurse notices a sudden cluster of patients arriving with severe vomiting and diarrhea from the same neighborhood. What action best reflects hazard identification?

question: A study tests if walking after surgery reduces hospital stay length. What is the dependent variable here?

options.A: The type of surgery performed
options.B: The nursing staff on duty
options.C: Walking after surgery
options.D: Length of the hospital stay

explanation: The dependent variable is the 'effect' or outcome you are measuring, which depends on the walking intervention. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T10#GNS217_U3_T10_h5)

question: What is the best way for a nursing team to share their successful hospital study with others?

options.A: Keeping the final report locked inside a private desk drawer
options.B: Presenting at a healthcare conference or publishing in a peer-reviewed journal
options.C: Posting raw data sheets on a public community notice board
options.D: Destroying all copies to protect hospital operational secrets

explanation: Good nursing knowledge is meant to be shared! Conferences and journals help spread great ideas so patient care improves everywhere. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h8)

question: Which of these clinical actions goes against the rules of rational drug use?

options.A: Prescribing strong broad-spectrum antibiotics for a simple viral upper respiratory infection
options.B: Educating a diabetic patient on the correct technique for self-administering insulin
options.C: Administering a standard dose of paracetamol for a documented fever in an adult
options.D: Checking a patient's kidney function before starting a new maintenance medication

explanation: Remember: antibiotics fight bacteria, not viruses! Giving them for a simple cold or viral infection wastes medicine and causes drug resistance. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T1#GNS215_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why is it a mistake for nurses to rely only on hospital admission records when assessing community mental health needs?

options.A: Hospital records are always legally classified as confidential
options.B: Community members prefer filling out long online surveys instead
options.C: It misses people suffering in silence who never seek formal medical care
options.D: Medical staff rarely document mental health diagnoses accurately

explanation: Hospital data only shows those who made it to a facility, ignoring a large population of struggling individuals who stay at home. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the main goal of using the 'teach-back' method when educating a patient?

options.A: To ensure the physician documented the correct diagnosis in the chart
options.B: To confirm that the patient truly understands the instructions in their own words
options.C: To test the patient's long-term memory after a neurological injury
options.D: To give the nurse a break from talking during the clinical consultation

explanation: Instead of asking 'Do you understand?' (where they'll just say yes), teach-back has them explain it back to you. It catches any misunderstandings instantly! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h7)

question: What is a major difference between standard examination gloves and surgical gloves?

options.A: Surgical gloves are strictly sterile and have longer cuffs
options.B: Examination gloves are always thicker and tougher
options.C: Examination gloves come in precise numbered hand sizes
options.D: Surgical gloves are only used for drawing blood

explanation: Surgical gloves are sterile and feature longer cuffs to cover your gown sleeves, keeping the operating field completely germ-free. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h3)

question: During a weaning trial, which sign tells you that the patient is struggling and needs ventilator support put back on?

options.A: A stable heart rate of 80 beats per minute
options.B: Use of accessory muscles and heavy sweating
options.C: An oxygen saturation level remaining at 96 percent
options.D: Calm restfulness with normal breathing rhythm

explanation: If you see a patient sweating, working hard with their neck and chest muscles, and breathing frantically, their muscles are exhausted. It's time to put the machine back on support! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T6#GNS315_U3_T6_h7)

question: Why does recovery from surgery continue for weeks or months after the skin stitches are removed?

options.A: Patients are usually restricted to liquid diets for six months
options.B: Deep internal tissues take weeks to months to regain full tensile strength
options.C: External healing is just a cosmetic illusion with no internal progress
options.D: The body stops absorbing any nutrients once the skin closes

explanation: Spot on! Even though the outside skin looks fine, the deeper muscles and tissues take much longer to get their full strength back. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h7)

question: What is the purpose of binding the chest with cloth after applying heat during breast ironing?

options.A: To hold medicinal herbal leaves in place
options.B: To absorb sweat from the heated stones
options.C: To keep the chest warm during cold weather
options.D: To physically restrict future breast growth

explanation: Tight binding is used alongside heat to prevent the breast tissue from expanding outward. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h3)

question: A patient who previously had a secretive abortion now struggles with recurrent miscarriages in her second trimester. What underlying issue should you suspect?

options.A: Primary ovarian failure due to hormonal imbalances
options.B: Chronic renal failure from past chemical toxicity
options.C: Acquired uterine fibroids from retained tissue
options.D: Cervical incompetence from past traumatic dilation

explanation: If the cervix was forced open too aggressively during a past procedure, the tissues can become weak, causing it to open prematurely in later pregnancies. You'll learn to spot this history during antenatal booking! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h4)

question: Why can taking too many fat-soluble vitamins become dangerous?

options.A: All vitamins contain high levels of dangerous dietary sodium
options.B: Excess vitamins immediately turn into stored body fat
options.C: High vitamin levels completely stop normal digestion
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins can accumulate in the body and cause toxicity

explanation: Unlike water-soluble vitamins that wash right out, fat-soluble ones get stored in body tissues and can build up to harmful levels. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T005#GNS227_U4_T005_h6)

question: Which sign is a classic clue that a patient has a respiratory diphtheria infection?

options.A: Uncontrollable whooping sounds during inhalation
options.B: A fluid-filled rash covering the entire trunk
options.C: A thick grey membrane obstructing the throat
options.D: Severe painful muscle spasms and body arching

explanation: You nailed it! Diphtheria forms a tough, greyish membrane in the throat that can dangerousy block airflow and release toxins. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h4)

question: What is the primary male surgical sterilization procedure called?

options.A: Tubal ligation
options.B: Vasectomy
options.C: Orchiectomy
options.D: Prostatectomy

explanation: A vasectomy blocks or cuts the vas deferens tubes to prevent sperm from entering the semen. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is considered a simple, low-tech assistive device?

options.A: A computerized communication board
options.B: A manual reacher
options.C: A motorized wheelchair
options.D: A robotic rehabilitation suit

explanation: Great job! Low-tech devices are simple tools that don't need electricity or fancy computer chips to work. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which complication is most directly linked to sluggish blood flow in the legs of an immobile patient?

options.A: Orthostatic hypotension
options.B: Deep vein thrombosis
options.C: Peripheral neuropathy
options.D: Pulmonary edema

explanation: Immobility slows venous return from the lower extremities, which allows blood clots to form more easily in deep veins. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is the golden rule of triage when responding to a major disaster?

options.A: Treating every single injured person in the exact order of arrival
options.B: Doing the greatest good for the greatest number of people
options.C: Sending all critical patients to the nearest small clinic
options.D: Focusing entirely on saving the person with the highest social status

explanation: In a disaster with scarce supplies, we shift our mindset from individual care to saving as many lives as our resources can possibly reach. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h2)

question: When should you tie up and replace a medical waste bag?

options.A: Completely packed to the brim
options.B: One-quarter full
options.C: Three-quarters full
options.D: Whenever it starts to smell

explanation: Always tie bags when they are about 3/4 full. This leaves enough space to close them securely without tearing the plastic. [learn more](GST114_U6_T8#GST114_U6_T8_h4)

question: Why is it so important to set clear learning objectives right at the start of a training program?

options.A: To satisfy legal requirements without needing to teach any practical skills
options.B: To ensure the program takes exactly eight hours to complete without failure
options.C: To give participants a clear goal of what they should achieve by the end
options.D: To prevent experienced nurses from attending the educational session

explanation: Clear objectives act like a roadmap. They let both the teacher and you know exactly what key takeaways to expect by the end of the session. [learn more](GST321_U8_T8#GST321_U8_T8_h4)

question: Why do patients with poorly controlled diabetes often develop delayed stomach emptying (gastroparesis)?

options.A: High sugar levels destroy specific gut cells through sudden local infections
options.B: Excess sugar physically coats the stomach lining and blocks food
options.C: High blood sugar damages the nerves (like the vagus nerve) that tell stomach muscles to move
options.D: Diabetes causes the stomach to make too much mucus, slowing digestion down

explanation: Over time, high blood sugar harms delicate nerves around the body. When the vagus nerve gets damaged, it can't send proper signals to make the stomach muscles contract. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h4)

question: Who does the WHO injection safety strategy aim to protect?

options.A: Patients, healthcare workers, and the surrounding environment
options.B: Hospital administrators, pharmacists, and medical equipment sellers
options.C: Patient comfort, medication speed, and low treatment costs
options.D: Drug manufacturing companies, shipping agents, and local clinics

explanation: Think of the safety triad: protect the patient, protect yourself (the healthcare worker), and keep the environment safe from hazardous waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is the core goal of managing risks in home health nursing?

options.A: Removing all personal belongings from the patient's living room
options.B: Transferring every elderly client to a long-term care facility
options.C: Enforcing strict hospital rules in every residential house
options.D: Balancing client safety with personal dignity and independence

explanation: Great home care respects the patient's freedom and lifestyle while finding smart, practical ways to keep them safe. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T8#GNS324_U2_T8_h8)

question: What is the absolute first safety step a nurse must take before asking a patient about abuse?

options.A: Have another nurse witness the conversation
options.B: Administer a full neurological examination
options.C: Ensure the alleged abuser is out of the room
options.D: Notify local law enforcement immediately

explanation: Safety first! Never ask screening questions in front of the suspected abuser, or you could put the patient in immediate physical danger. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h5)

question: What hormone causes the rise in basal body temperature after ovulation?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Progesterone is a thermogenic hormone released after ovulation that slightly increases the basal body temperature. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T010#GNS226_U6_T010_h2)

question: Why do cooks love adding waterleaf to traditional Nigerian soups and stews?

options.A: It turns the broth into a solid gel when allowed to cool down
options.B: It serves as a strong preservative to keep soups from spoiling quickly
options.C: It acts as a natural thickening agent while adding moisture and vitamins
options.D: It completely replaces the need for adding palm oil to the pot

explanation: Spot on! Waterleaf breaks down nicely during cooking to give soups a rich texture while boosting the vitamin content. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T009#GNS227_U4_T009_h4)

question: A patient suddenly feels intense terror, chest pain, and a sense of doom that peaks within minutes. What condition matches this?

options.A: Generalized anxiety disorder
options.B: Social anxiety disorder
options.C: Specific phobia
options.D: Panic disorder

explanation: Exactly! Those sudden, terrifying rushes with strong physical signs are classic hallmarks of panic attacks seen in panic disorder. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T1#GNS324_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why do nurses focus on empowerment in Family Life Education?

options.A: It forces community members to adopt identical lifestyles
options.B: It ensures that nurses make all final decisions for clients
options.C: It helps learners build critical thinking for better choices
options.D: It prevents individuals from questioning health policies

explanation: Empowerment means giving people the tools to think for themselves so they can make the best health decisions for their own lives. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h2)

question: Why do many patients forget to mention their herbal supplements during a medication history interview?

options.A: Herbal products dissolve instantly and leave no trace in the body
options.B: Hospital regulations strictly forbid talking about traditional medicine
options.C: Nurses never ask about home remedies during admission
options.D: They consider supplements to be harmless food items rather than real drugs

explanation: Patients often view herbs as 'just food' or natural, so it doesn't cross their minds to report them as medications. That's why we always have to ask! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h6)

question: What is the primary public health goal of proper food storage?

options.A: To reduce the cost of grocery bills
options.B: To improve the taste of meals
options.C: To make cooking faster every day
options.D: To prevent foodborne illnesses

explanation: Keeping food properly stops harmful bacteria and germs from multiplying, which directly protects people from getting sick. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h1)

question: Why do organ transplant patients need to take immunosuppressive drugs long-term?

options.A: To prevent high blood pressure after surgery
options.B: To stop the immune system from rejecting the new organ
options.C: To help the surgical wound heal much faster
options.D: To help the new organ pump its own blood

explanation: Immunosuppressants act like a quiet button for the immune system, keeping it calm so it doesn't recognize and destroy the precious new donor tissue. [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h5)

question: What type of power does a nurse have simply because they were officially appointed as the shift charge nurse?

options.A: Referent power
options.B: Coercive power
options.C: Expert power
options.D: Legitimate power

explanation: Correct! Legitimate power comes directly from your official job title or position in the hospital hierarchy. [learn more](GST321_U3_T1#GST321_U3_T1_h5)

question: What are the three parts of the epidemiological triad used to study how diseases spread?

options.A: Infection, disease, and recovery
options.B: Pathogen, vector, and symptom
options.C: Agent, host, and environment
options.D: Human, animal, and bacteria

explanation: Think of the triad as a stool with three legs: the infectious agent, the susceptible host, and the environment. All three must interact for an infection to take root! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T79#GNS214_U1_T79_h1)

question: What is the name of the age-related muscle loss condition that often affects nutritional assessments in older adults?

options.A: Sarcopenia
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Atherosclerosis
options.D: Hypertrophy

explanation: Well done! Sarcopenia is the gradual, natural decrease in muscle mass and strength as people age, which changes what normal body composition looks like for them. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T003#GNS227_U5_T003_h7)

question: When we say a daily diet has "adequacy," what does that mainly mean?

options.A: Consuming fewer calories than you burn each day
options.B: Limiting your food intake to only one meal type
options.C: Buying expensive imported food items regularly
options.D: Eating enough essential nutrients to meet bodily needs

explanation: Spot on! Adequacy simply means your diet gives you enough energy and all the vital nutrients your body needs to stay healthy and strong. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h1)

question: What is the standard defaulter rate commonly measured in routine immunization programs?

options.A: The drop-out rate between the first and last doses of a series
options.B: The percentage of expired vaccine vials found in the fridge
options.C: The total number of babies born in a hospital annually
options.D: The daily count of pregnant women attending antenatal care

explanation: The drop-out rate—such as the difference between Penta 1 and Penta 3 uptake—is the standard metric used to measure defaulting. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h6)

question: Why do researchers use exclusion criteria when picking study participants?

options.A: To keep out factors that could mess up the study results or harm the patient
options.B: To remove the need for getting informed consent from patients
options.C: To increase the total number of people in the research study
options.D: To make sure every nurse in the hospital gets a chance to participate

explanation: Well done! Exclusion criteria act like a safety guard, keeping out things that might confuse your results or put a vulnerable patient at risk. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h3)

question: Why must healthcare resources always be carefully managed and rationed?

options.A: Governments prefer to spend money on education instead of health
options.B: Patients rarely use the medical services provided to them
options.C: Medical equipment is always too expensive to manufacture
options.D: Resources are limited while human healthcare needs are infinite

explanation: You'll see this a lot in practice: money, beds, and staff are finite, but sick patients always need care. That gap means we have to make smart choices! [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why must a patient taking methotrexate for an ectopic pregnancy avoid folic acid supplements?

options.A: Folic acid masks the warning signs of internal bleeding in the abdomen
options.B: Folic acid speeds up the breakdown of liver enzymes and causes jaundice
options.C: Folic acid causes severe allergic reactions when mixed with hormone drugs
options.D: Folic acid counteracts the medication and helps the ectopic tissue continue to grow

explanation: Methotrexate works by blocking folic acid, which rapidly dividing cells need; taking extra folic acid stops the medication from working properly. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h7)

question: What does 'segregation of duties' mean when managing DRF cash?

options.A: Different people should handle drug dispensing and cash collection
options.B: Auditors must check the pharmacy books once every year
options.C: Suppliers must deliver drugs before payment is approved
options.D: Pharmacists must work morning and night shifts alternately

explanation: Exactly! When one person hands out drugs and another person collects the money, it creates a checks-and-balances system that prevents theft and keeps everyone honest. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T3#GNS215_U3_T3_h2)

question: When might a doctor choose a barium enema instead of a standard colonoscopy?

options.A: When the patient needs an immediate tissue biopsy of a mass
options.B: When a tight narrowing (stricture) stops the colonoscope from passing through
options.C: When looking at blood vessels is the only goal
options.D: When the patient has an active bowel tear needing emergency surgery

explanation: Liquid barium can flow past narrow spots that a camera scope cannot safely squeeze through, helping doctors see what is happening further up the bowel. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h2)

question: At 20 weeks pregnant, a patient's serum creatinine level is 1.0 mg/dL. What does this result suggest?

options.A: Severe maternal dehydration
options.B: Normal kidney function for pregnancy
options.C: Potential underlying renal impairment
options.D: A normal non-pregnant baseline

explanation: Because kidney filtration speeds up during pregnancy, normal creatinine levels actually drop below 1.0 mg/dL. A value of 1.0 mg/dL means the kidneys might not be clearing waste as well as they should right now. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h2)

question: What is a key part of effective palliative communication?

options.A: Avoiding all discussions about death
options.B: Rushing through explanations to save time
options.C: Making decisions without consulting the family
options.D: Active listening to patient and family concerns

explanation: Listening is our greatest nursing tool. When we truly listen, we build trust and make sure our care matches what the patient and family really want. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T2#GNS321_U4_T2_h6)

question: Which document tells a nurse NOT to start CPR on an unresponsive patient?

options.A: A general medical insurance policy
options.B: A valid do-not-resuscitate order
options.C: A verbal request from a distant relative
options.D: A standard hospital admission form

explanation: Always respect patient wishes! A signed and valid Do-Not-Resuscitate (DNR) order or advance directive legally stops us from initiating CPR. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T7#GNS315_U3_T7_h9)

question: About how many extra calories a day are needed in the later stages of pregnancy?

options.A: Three hundred calories
options.B: Two thousand calories
options.C: One thousand calories
options.D: Fifty calories

explanation: Spot on! An extra 300 calories a day—like a small, nourishing snack—is usually all it takes to fuel the final trimesters. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T008#GNS227_U2_T008_h2)

question: Which behavior is very common for a patient dealing with illness anxiety?

options.A: Consistently ignoring all physical pain without worry
options.B: Repeatedly checking the body for lumps or abnormalities
options.C: Voluntarily stopping all interactions with healthcare workers
options.D: Seeking immediate surgery for nonexistent conditions

explanation: You will often see patients engage in compulsive checking—like constantly scanning their skin, checking their pulse, or probing for swollen lymph nodes. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T8#GNS314_U2_T8_h2)

question: A patient is feeling completely overwhelmed after just finding out they have diabetes. Which counselling approach fits best?

options.A: Vocational counselling
options.B: Financial investment advice
options.C: Personal-social counselling
options.D: Educational guidance

explanation: Dealing with the emotional shock and lifestyle changes of a new diagnosis falls right under personal-social and emotional support. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T11#GNS124_U5_T11_h4)

question: Which of these is a healthy, adaptive way for a client to cope with a tough health diagnosis?

options.A: Relying heavily on unprescribed sedatives
options.B: Denying that the illness exists altogether
options.C: Focusing on remaining abilities and maintaining humor
options.D: Isolating oneself completely from family members

explanation: Finding ways to laugh, adapt, and focus on what they can still do helps clients roll with the punches. That's true resilience! [learn more](GNS324_U2_T2#GNS324_U2_T2_h4)

question: How does a community health nurse's role differ from a hospital nurse?

options.A: The community nurse has no responsibility for patient health outcomes
options.B: The community nurse spends all shift managing mechanical ventilators
options.C: The community nurse strictly follows rigid hospital visiting rules
options.D: The community nurse focuses more on education, advocacy, and resource linkage

explanation: You nailed it! Community nurses shine by teaching populations and connecting families to health resources around them. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h6)

question: How does having a larger risk pool help a health insurance scheme?

options.A: It balances out the costs between healthy and sick members more effectively
options.B: It ensures that taxes are completely abolished
options.C: It removes the need for patients to ever visit a pharmacy
options.D: It allows the hospital to hire foreign doctors exclusively

explanation: The more healthy people join the pool, the easier it is to cover the medical bills of the few who fall sick. Safety truly lies in numbers! [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h3)

question: A researcher wants to see if night-shift fatigue relates to medication errors among nurses, without changing their shifts. What design is this?

options.A: Historical qualitative
options.B: True experimental
options.C: Non-experimental
options.D: Quasi-experimental

explanation: Spot on! Because work schedules aren't being altered or manipulated, it's a non-experimental study observing everyday realities. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T4#GNS224_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is a very common feeling for someone newly admitted to a hospital?

options.A: Complete emotional indifference to surroundings
options.B: Anxiety and a sense of vulnerability
options.C: Total independence over institutional schedules
options.D: Overwhelming joy regarding hospital routines

explanation: True story! Hospitals can feel strange and intimidating, so it's normal for newly admitted patients to feel a bit anxious and exposed. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h3)

question: If a pain-relief trial shows patients actually felt *more* distressed after the new method, what should the discussion do?

options.A: Conclude that the nursing profession should stop measuring pain entirely
options.B: Change the data labels so distress looks like pain relief
options.C: Examine what factors might have caused this surprising increase in distress
options.D: Publish the paper immediately without mentioning the pain scores

explanation: Spot on! We can't hide unexpected outcomes. Facing them head-on helps protect patients and improves future care. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T5#GNS224_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the main law protecting the rights of children in Nigeria?

options.A: The Adult Criminal Code
options.B: The Child Rights Act
options.C: The Public Land Decree
options.D: The National Health Insurance Act

explanation: Spot on! The Child Rights Act is the key legal framework safeguarding the welfare and special protection of minors in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h7)

question: Which condition is the most common immediate complication following a thoracocentesis?

options.A: Acute liver damage
options.B: Pneumothorax
options.C: Pulmonary embolism
options.D: Severe kidney failure

explanation: Accidental puncture of the lung surface allows air to enter the pleural space, resulting in a pneumothorax. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h7)

question: Why does safe motherhood include mental and social well-being alongside physical health?

options.A: Because total health affects a woman's ability to care for herself and her baby
options.B: Because mental health issues only occur after delivery
options.C: Because physical health cannot be measured during pregnancy
options.D: Because social status is the only cause of maternal mortality

explanation: A holistic view of health recognizes that emotional and social support are just as vital as physical care for a mother and her child. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h1)

question: What is the main job of self-tolerance in our immune system?

options.A: To prevent the immune system from attacking healthy body tissue
options.B: To destroy foreign invaders like bacteria and viruses
options.C: To increase the production of red blood cells
options.D: To help white blood cells mature in the lymph nodes

explanation: Think of self-tolerance as the immune system's security check. It helps white blood cells recognize our own body parts so they don't mistakenly attack healthy organs! [learn more](GST114_U4_T8#GST114_U4_T8_h1)

question: What happens when the lower oesophageal sphincter fails to close properly?

options.A: Air builds up rapidly in the upper airway
options.B: Digestive enzymes destroy the small intestine
options.C: Swallowed food gets trapped in the throat
options.D: Stomach acid flows backward into the tube

explanation: Think of this sphincter as a one-way gate. When it stays loose, irritating stomach contents can easily splash back upward, causing that familiar burning feeling. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is the main limitation of an Electronic Medical Record (EMR) compared to an EHR?

options.A: It is usually restricted to a single facility or clinic
options.B: It cannot be viewed by registered nurses or doctors
options.C: It only contains billing information and insurance forms
options.D: It is always written on paper rather than typed digitally

explanation: Good job! An EMR is great for one specific clinic's digital files, but it doesn't easily share that info with outside hospitals. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h3)

question: How do people usually catch paragonimiasis?

options.A: Eating raw or undercooked crabs and crayfish
options.B: Inhaling dust contaminated with dried parasite eggs
options.C: Being bitten by infected blackflies near rivers
options.D: Drinking untreated water from open streams

explanation: Exactly right! It all usually comes down to diet—eating freshwater crabs or crayfish that haven't been cooked enough to kill the parasite. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T26#GNS313_U2_T26_h3)

question: A nurse wants to make sure new health posters are clear before printing thousands of copies. What should she do?

options.A: Ask doctors in the capital city to review the picture quality
options.B: Distribute all the posters immediately to save transport costs
options.C: Pre-test the posters with a small group of local community members
options.D: Translate the medical text into Latin for a more professional look

explanation: Brilliant! Always pre-test your materials with the target audience first to catch confusing pictures or messages before mass printing. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why does the brain send balance signals from the inner ear down to the spinal cord?

options.A: To automatically adjust posture and keep the body from falling
options.B: To lubricate the joints in the arms and legs
options.C: To manage conscious thoughts about spatial direction
options.D: To control the speed and rhythm of heartbeat and breathing

explanation: This reflex pathway lets your muscles make instant adjustments so you stay upright without having to think about it! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which body carries the primary duty of passing national disability rights laws?

options.A: Local volunteer charities
options.B: Private pharmaceutical firms
options.C: Individual patient families
options.D: The national government

explanation: The government sets the legal foundation and framework needed to protect and support citizens living with disabilities across the country. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h5)

question: Why is giving large volumes of IV fluids dangerous for a patient in cardiogenic shock?

options.A: It causes an immediate drop in body temperature and shivering
options.B: It dissolves blood clots in the coronary arteries too fast
options.C: It triggers a severe allergic reaction in the blood vessels
options.D: It worsens heart failure by overloading a weak heart that cannot pump the fluid

explanation: A failing heart cannot handle extra fluid volume, which leads to fluid backing up into the lungs and worsening respiratory failure. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why should you advise a new mother NOT to start a crash weight-loss diet right after delivery while breastfeeding?

options.A: It can decrease milk volume and deplete her own nutrient stores
options.B: It will cause the baby to develop an allergy to breast milk
options.C: It stops the uterus from shrinking back to normal size
options.D: It causes immediate postpartum depression

explanation: Her body needs good nourishment to recover from childbirth and keep up a healthy milk supply for her baby. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h6)

question: Why is a silent chest in a patient with severe asthma considered a dangerous emergency?

options.A: It means air is no longer moving in or out of the lungs
options.B: It is a normal finding during deep sleep
options.C: It shows that the inhaler medication worked successfully
options.D: It indicates the asthma attack has completely resolved

explanation: A silent chest means the airways are so tight or blocked that air cannot move at all, which signals immediate respiratory arrest. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of home health care documentation?

options.A: To serve as a marketing tool for private agencies
options.B: To replace verbal reports between the nurse and family
options.C: To determine the salary of the visiting community nurse
options.D: To provide a clear clinical and legal history of care

explanation: Documentation serves as an official record of the client's status and the care provided, which is essential for clinical continuity and legal protection. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h1)

question: What happens right in the center of an old TB tubercle as the infection sits there?

options.A: Caseous necrosis or cheese-like tissue death
options.B: Conversion of bacteria into normal flora
options.C: Rapid regeneration of healthy lung tissue
options.D: Calcification into solid bone-like structures

explanation: As the battle inside the tubercle continues, the center part of the tissue dies and turns into a soft, crumbly substance that looks a bit like cheese—hence 'caseous necrosis'. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of running joint disaster drills with local and national agencies beforehand?

options.A: It guarantees that weather events will completely bypass the region
options.B: It removes all physical dangers associated with frontline rescue work
options.C: Familiarity with command structures helps eliminate bureaucratic delays during a real emergency
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing medical equipment

explanation: Practicing together builds teamwork and trust, so everyone coordinates smoothly when every second counts. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h6)

question: A patient feels a quick cramp during an endometrial biopsy in the clinic. What do you tell her?

options.A: Administer a full dose of general intravenous anesthesia immediately
options.B: Tell the patient that the procedure was performed incorrectly by the doctor
options.C: Call the emergency surgical team immediately for suspected uterine rupture
options.D: Explain that temporary uterine cramping is a normal response to tissue sampling

explanation: Well done! Passing tools through the cervix and taking a little tissue sample naturally causes brief, passing cramps. Reassuring your patient makes a huge difference. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why does the stomach have an extra layer of muscle compared to other parts of the digestive tract?

options.A: To allow vigorous multi-directional churning of solid food
options.B: To absorb nutrients directly into the bloodstream very quickly
options.C: To store extra blood supply for active digestive processes
options.D: To prevent digestive enzymes from burning through the wall

explanation: Food isn't always liquid! That extra muscle layer gives the stomach extra power to twist and mash solid food into a smooth mixture. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T3#GNS121_U1_T3_h2)
